event_check: NOT CONFIRMED, and probably not today. Hingham does not pre-announce release dates. Its 2025 releases came on the second Friday after quarter-end: Apr 11, Jul 11 and Oct 10 2025 (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/31851644/hingham-savings-reports-first-quarter-2025-results, https://finviz.com/news/101786/hingham-savings-reports-second-quarter-2025-results, https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20262448-hingham-savings-reports-third-quarter-2025-results). Every 2026 release came on the THIRD Friday, 16-17 days after quarter-end: Jan 16 (https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/hingham-savings-reports-2025-results-2026-01-16), Apr 17 (https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-04/68234150-hingham-institution-for-savings-hingham-savings-reports-first-quarter-2026-results-399.htm) and Jul 17 (https://www.hinghamsavings.com/assets/2026/07/PRESS-RELEASE-Q2-2026.pdf). In April and July 2026 the second Friday (Apr 10, Jul 10) was available and was skipped. The 2026 pattern therefore points to Fri 2026-10-16, which is outside this window. The aggregators disagree: NextEarningsDate projects 10/9 from the 2025 cadence, EarningsWhispers has 10/15. No Q3 2026 release was findable at 13:32 ET. My estimate is about 25% that the release lands today at 16:01 ET. The findings below are filed for that case and sized by that probability.
conviction_note: The event is unconfirmed and most likely lands on 2026-10-16, outside the window. Conditional on a print today, the evidence roughly offsets: a probable Q3 mark-to-market loss on the equity book and a Fed hike that likely stalls the NIM expansion, against the Q2 Fiserv one-off dropping out, a short base near 16% of float and DC credit workouts going to sale. Each finding is weighted by the ~25% chance of a print today, so impact_sum is about 0 and p_up is 50.

The past-year peak was 343.2K on 2026-02-13, around the Wolfpack report. IBKR borrow fee was 0.8% at the 2026-10-08 close with 3.0K shares available (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/hifs/). The stock is down 6.24% over 20 days, 12% below its 52-week high and 15.6% above its 52-week low, and it traded up 1.8% intraday today.

findings.finding: The equity securities book probably took a Q3 mark-to-market LOSS. Marketable equities were $155.5m at 6/30/26, about 32% of $482m equity, and Alphabet was the largest holding (10-Q note 5). The rest is financial-services stocks. GOOGL closed 357.37 on 6/30 and 344.08 on 9/30 (−3.7%), and KBWB went 92.98 to 87.23 (−6.2%). At −4 to −6% on the book, the after-tax loss is about $4.5-7m, or −$2 to −$3 a share. GAAP EPS would then be roughly $2-3, against $11.49 in Q2 2026 and $7.85 in Q3 2025, while core EPS is unaffected. Conditional on a print today the size is −0.3; weighted by about 25% probability of a print in the window it is −0.08.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 brought a +168% YoY GAAP EPS jump driven by equity gains. HIFS closed 295.14 on 7/17 (release at 16:01) and 291.63 on 7/20, −1.2% (https://www.financialcontent.com/quote/NQ%3AHIFS/historical?Month=10&Year=2025&Range=1). Q1 2026 brought a $9.9m equity loss and GAAP EPS down 60% YoY. Holders look through the GAAP line.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-09 if the release comes at 16:01 ET today, giving a 10-12 close; most likely 2026-10-16, which is outside the window
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is computable from public prices, but the holdings beyond Alphabet are not disclosed quarterly, so nobody can state the size of the mark. HIFS has no sell-side model publishing a GAAP number. If the loss were priced, I would expect a visible pre-print discount relative to book. Instead the stock trades at about 1.27x the 6/30 book of $230.83, with no visible discount.
findings.independence: GOOGL monthly closes (https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/GOOGL/price) and KBWB monthly closes (https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/KBWB/price) are price series, not a company number. This finding shares the 10-Q with no other finding.

findings.finding: The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, and projected another this year. CME had priced the hike above 90% beforehand, so short-term rate expectations rose through Q3. Hingham is liability-sensitive: $1.405bn of FHLB advances and $1.915bn of wholesale funds against $2.084bn of retail and commercial deposits. Its NIM expansion was already slowing: +15bp in Q1 to 2.04%, then +10bp in Q2 to 2.14%, with the cost of interest-bearing liabilities falling only 5bp in Q2 against 14bp in Q1. Q3 NIM is likely flat to only slightly up, and Q4 NIM faces a reversal. That would break the narrative of core returns 'improving materially over time'. Conditional on a print the size is −0.6; probability-weighted it is −0.15.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no reaction history in the baseline (FDIC filer). Q1 2026's +15bp NIM step and Q2's +10bp step came with a flat core EPS ($4.79, then $4.82), and the stock fell −1.2% after the Q2 print.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-09 if released today; most likely 2026-10-16, which is outside the window
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is −6.2% over 20 days and KBWB fell 8.5% in September. What is not priced is the company-level number: Hingham does not guide, so its Q3 NIM and cost of funds are seen for the first time in the release. If the stall were priced, HIFS would have lagged the bank index in September, and it did not: HIFS ran 288 (8/31) to 283 (9/30), −2%, against KBWB −8.5%.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 release (https://www.hinghamsavings.com/assets/2026/07/PRESS-RELEASE-Q2-2026.pdf) shows the slowing deceleration in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities. The macro-to-company transmission is a proxy that the company has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 operating expenses included a $928k one-off Fiserv termination fee and a $201k check-fraud loss. Q2 efficiency was 37.46% against 34.87% in Q1, and opex/assets was 0.79% against 0.69%. About $1.13m pre-tax, roughly $0.37 a share after tax, falls away in Q3 unless the Q2 Technologies online-banking go-live in 2H26 brings new conversion costs. Core EPS is therefore mechanically helped against the Q2 base. Conditional size +0.3; probability-weighted +0.08.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print carried the fee in core and the stock moved −1.2%. There is no other history on this line.

findings.independence: This shares a document with the credit finding (the same Q2 release). Nothing independent points the same way.

findings.finding: Washington DC credit workouts were moving to cash after quarter-end. The Q2 release says the bank 'placed two additional properties under agreement shortly after quarter end' and is marketing the rest of the nine foreclosed properties, booked at no loss on contemporaneous appraisals. It sold its $3.7m construction-loan interest at no loss. NPAs were 0.78% of assets at 6/30, against 0.87% at 3/31. The $30.6m DC development-site CRE loan, carrying a $2.5m specific reserve, is unresolved. A Q3 with sales at or above carrying value would answer the February 2026 Wolfpack thesis; any loss on the $30.6m credit would revive it. Conditional size +0.2 (two-sided); probability-weighted +0.05.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Wolfpack report of 2026-02-25 alleged more than $125m of undisclosed NPLs and foreclosures. The stock fell about 8% that day (secondary summary). The bank's rebuttal came on 2026-02-26 (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/452251/recent-reporting-regarding-hingham). There has been no realised loss since.

findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is still near 296K shares (8 days to cover). If the market had accepted that the DC book is resolving at no loss, the short base would have come down, and it rose 10.6% in early September.
findings.independence: This shares a document with the Fiserv finding. The February 2026 bank rebuttal (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/452251/recent-reporting-regarding-hingham) is consistent with the bank's position but is not independent.

findings.finding: The short base is crowded and rebuilt into the print. It was 295.7K shares at 9/15, up from 267.3K at 8/31, with 8.0 days to cover, roughly 13-16% of float. Average volume is only 38K shares a day. A clean credit quarter would give the activist short little new material, and the thin float makes a squeeze plausible, while a credit loss would feed the short. Conditional size +0.4; probability-weighted +0.10.
